title: Tenant & Landlord Rights — Security Deposit, Eviction, and Rental Laws in India
source: Model Tenancy Act 2021 & State Rent Control Acts
content:
Tenancy relationships in India are governed by State Rent Control Acts and the Model Tenancy Act (MTA) 2021 adopted by various state legislatures, alongside the Transfer of Property Act 1882.

Rental Agreement (Lease Deed): A lease agreement exceeding 11 months must be registered under the Registration Act 1908. Most residential tenancies are executed for 11 months to avoid compulsory registration, though an unregistered agreement remains valid evidence of tenancy terms in court.

Security Deposit Refund: Under the Model Tenancy Act 2021, security deposits for residential premises are capped at a maximum of two months' rent. Landlords are legally required to refund the security deposit to the tenant within one month of vacating the premises, after deducting legitimate dues for damages beyond normal wear and tear or unpaid utility bills/rent.

Unreasonable Withholding of Security Deposit: If a landlord unlawfully retains the deposit without valid written justification or itemised deduction bills, the tenant has legal remedies: (1) Send a formal Legal Notice demanding refund within 15 days, (2) File a summary suit under Order 37 of Civil Procedure Code (CPC) for recovery of money with interest, or (3) Approach the Rent Authority / Rent Tribunal established under the local Rent Act.

Illegal Eviction: A landlord cannot forcibly evict a tenant, disconnect essential utility services (electricity, water, gas), or lock premises without a valid court or Rent Authority order. Cut-off of essential services by the landlord is a punishable offence under Rent Control laws.

Notice Period for Vacating: Both landlord and tenant must adhere to the notice period specified in the registered or executed agreement (typically 1 to 3 months). In the absence of an agreed notice period, Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act mandates 15 days' notice for month-to-month residential leases.

Maintenance Responsibilities: Unless agreed otherwise, structural repairs are the landlord's responsibility, while routine day-to-day minor maintenance is borne by the tenant.
